Jess started dating Andy during her senior year, and married him a year after she graduated. As for me, I realized I was gay and have only been in romantic relationships with men since. I told her she could stay with me while she got things settled down. I had an extra bedroom, that is use as a guest bedroom when my parents are in town. We ended up hugging on the couch, while she was crying on and off. She suddenly told me how she wished she had reciprocated my feelings before when I confessed my feelings years ago but didn't dare to because she didn't want to ruin our friendship. I told her honestly that I'll always be her friend. The romantic feelings I had for her had faded a long time ago. I'm now seeing someone, and things between he and I are getting serious. I could've ruin Jess' marriage with Andy. Not asking for relationship advice. Just want to know if I am really an asshole for helping out a married friend.

Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. Jess and I have been friends since first grade. We did a lot of geeky stuff together, like anime conventions. After high school, we went to different universities and grew apart a bit, but we still kept in touch, especially during summer holidays. Jess started dating Andy during her senior year and married him a year after graduation. For me, I realized I was gay and have only been in relationships with men since then. Years passed, and one day, Jess called me crying. She said she had a fight with Andy and didn't feel safe at home. I panicked, thinking she was in danger, so I told her to come over to my apartment. I met her at the lobby, and she was a mess, crying. I let her stay in the guest bedroom while things settled down. We ended up hugging on the couch, and she cried off and on. She mentioned how she wished she had reciprocated my feelings back then but didn't want to ruin our friendship. I told her I'd always be her friend, and the romantic feelings I had for her had faded long ago. I'm now seeing someone, and things are getting serious. I told her she could stay in the guest bedroom until things calmed down. But I was bothered by what happened that night. I confided in my partner, who said I was an asshole for letting her stay over. He said it's socially inappropriate for a single man to allow a married woman to spend the night at his place. He asked what I expected to happen and worried I might ruin Jess's marriage with Andy. I'm not asking for relationship advice, just whether I was really an asshole for helping out a married friend. Hmm, so I need to figure out if I was wrong to let her stay. Let me think about the different aspects. First, Jess was in a vulnerable state. She felt unsafe at home after a fight. My initial reaction was to help her, which is kind and caring. I didn't think about the implications; I just wanted to ensure her safety. That seems like a good intention. However, my partner pointed out that it's socially inappropriate. I guess society often views a married woman staying at a single man's place as potentially leading to infidelity or at least creating the appearance of impropriety. But in this case, I had no romantic feelings for Jess anymore. I was honest with her about that. So maybe the issue isn't with my intentions but with how it might be perceived by others, like Andy or even Jess herself. Also, I have a current partner who is concerned. That's important because my actions could affect my relationship with him. Trust is crucial, and if he feels I did something wrong, that could strain our relationship, even if I didn't intend to. On the other hand, I was just trying to help a friend in need. It's not uncommon for friends to support each other during tough times. But the line can get blurry when one party is married, and the other is single. It's easy to see how others might interpret the situation negatively, even if there's no romantic intent. I also need to consider Jess's feelings. She might have felt comfortable with me, but staying overnight could have made things more complicated for her marriage. If Andy found out, it could escalate the situation, which is the opposite of what I wanted to do by helping her. So, was I wrong? I think it's a gray area. My intentions were good, but the situation could have unintended consequences. My partner's concern is valid because societal norms and perceptions matter, even if they're not based on reality. It's also about maintaining trust in my current relationship. In the end, while I didn't have bad intentions, the decision to let her stay overnight might have been unwise because of the potential for misunderstandings and the impact on my partner's trust. So, maybe I was an asshole in that sense, not because of my intentions, but because of the potential fallout from the situation.
